formattedAddress: 104, Taiwan, Taipei City, Zhongshan District, Chenggong Village, ZhiFu Rd, 8號入口於典華停車場後方木門處

text.text:
This café has been on my to-visit list forever, and today I finally made it 🤍

Chalet V is the definition of fancy but cozy. The high ceilings make the space feel so open and elegant, and they even have a dedicated area for wedding ceremonies — such a beautiful touch 💍

Their menu has several coffee options, but I went with a classic Americano.
☕ NT$120 only, which honestly surprised me — especially considering the quality of their coffee beans, better than many cafés around.

The brunch menu is rich and well-designed. I ordered the herbal salmon, served with sautéed vegetables and quinoa — a clean, healthy, and satisfying plate 🥗
It costs NT$580. I was expecting a slightly larger portion of salmon for the price, but the flavor was really good, so I still enjoyed it.

Service was fast and smooth, and I loved the open kitchen — watching the chefs prepare the food makes the experience even better 👀✨
Restrooms were clean, and every staff member was kind, professional, and attentive 💕

This is definitely a place I’ll come back to again.
If you love beautiful cafés, good food, and quality coffee, you’ll love this spot.

text.text: Chalet V is a hidden gem. The flavors were perfectly balanced, portions generous, and the ingredients clearly top-notch. The staff were welcoming and attentive without being intrusive. It’s rare to find a place that combines such good food with a warm, inviting atmosphere—I’ll definitely be coming back!

text.text:
Had a lovely brunch at CHALET V. The honeycomb praline pancakes were decadent,and topped with the perfect amount of sweetness. The kale & mushrooms with truffle eggs tartine was well-balanced, earthy and rich, with just the right touch of truffle.

Cozy place, chill music, and really friendly staff.

A little on the pricey side 💸, but everything felt thoughtfully made and beautifully presented.

text.text:
I recently checked out Chalet V in Dazhi, Taipei, and it was such a nice surprise. The place feels like a mountain cabin tucked into the city, wooden interiors, big windows, and a chill outdoor space with lots of greenery. It's quiet, cozy, and honestly feels like a little escape from the busy streets.

Bonus points for being pet-friendly! I saw a few people with their dogs on the lawn, which makes it a great weekend hangout spot if you have pets.

It’s a bit hidden—entrance is kind of around the side near Dianhua Plaza—but totally worth the find. I’d recommend going on a weekday since they close on weekends for private events.

Overall, a great place to relax, eat well, and enjoy a quiet vibe in the city.
